uncited: The Eight Logical Memories Architecture is a memory layout optimization for dense volume rendering that maps voxel data to physical SDRAM banks to minimize access latency.
It solves the problem of bank conflicts and high switching times by grouping eight neighboring subcubes into a logical unit that spans two physical SDRAM devices, assuming four banks per SDRAM.

It sets itself apart from the parent [Voxel Memory Bank Allocation and Miniblock Organization](1638-voxel-memory-bank-allocation-and-miniblock-organization.md) by introducing a hierarchical grouping of banks into logical memories, and from its sibling [Skewed Memory Organization for Conflict-Free Ray Access](2351-skewed-memory-organization-for-conflict-free-ray-access.md) by relying on coordinated precharging rather than spatial skewing to handle ray traversal.
*   **Output:** A physical memory layout mapping logical memory banks (A-H) to SDRAM devices and a command sequence for ray traversal.
The architecture organizes memory into logical banks labeled A through H. Each logical bank corresponds to a specific region of the voxel space.
*   **Devices per Logical Memory:** Two 16-bit wide SDRAM devices are required to service one logical memory (providing the 32-bit width).
*   **Banks per SDRAM:** 4 (labeled A, B, C, D in the source text for a single device).
*   **Logical Bank Size:** Each individual logical bank (A-H) covers a volume of $16^3$ voxels.
*   **Precharge Cube Size:** The cube encompassing the neighborhood requiring a precharge command is $32^3$ voxels.
**Map Subcubes to Banks:** Divide the voxel space into subcubes.
Place neighboring subcubes in the x, y, and z directions into neighboring SDRAM banks.
**Distribute Across SDRAMs:** Assign three of the neighboring subcubes to the same physical SDRAM device.
Assign the remaining four neighboring subcubes to a second physical SDRAM device.
This assumes each SDRAM has 4 internal banks.
**Construct Logical Memory:** Combine the banks from the two SDRAMs to form one logical memory unit containing 8 logical banks (A-H).
**Issue Precharge Commands:** When a ray traverses into the neighborhood of these eight logical banks, issue a precharge command across all eight banks simultaneously.

**Optimize Switching:** By precharging all banks in the neighborhood, switching between any two banks within the logical memory takes only the time of a bank activate command, rather than a precharge-activate sequence.
*   **Boundary Conditions:** The precharge command is issued based on the ray entering the neighborhood of the eight banks.
